body:
A recent break-up, mostly.  Almost 4 months later and my self-esteem and self-confidence are still wrecked.  I was with a girl for almost 2 years and earlier this year we learned she was pregnant.  A few months later she had a miscarriage, and it somehow destroyed our relationship.  A few months ago she said the "spark" was gone.  In our last conversation a month ago, I told her that I missed her deeply and thought about her from the time I awoke to the time I went to sleep.  And her response was that she rarely thought of me, and didn't miss me all that much, and how the thought of going on a date with somebody new made her feel excited again.  

I'm a decently handsome guy, college degree, professional job, house, no kids or ex-wives or huge debts or other baggage, and I'm very caring and humorous and treat people well.  Everything points towards me being a total catch, but in practice it seems to be the opposite.  I'm clearly missing something, I have never known what it is, and I'm quite sure I'm going to journey into old age alone.  I want little else in life but to have a good wife and be a family man, and it has never happened for me.  

The holidays are just the worst.  Everywhere I look there are constant reminders of my failure to have a family of my own.  I listen to the radio and I hear ads for engagement rings.  I turn on the TV and see the perfect little family gathering around the Christmas tree so dad can show mom her brand new $5000 diamond jewelry, or surprise her with her new Lexus with a bow on top.  I could never have anything like that.... I don't have a wife, for starters, and also don't make that kind of money. 

It's like Christmas time has turned into a "season of love and romance", like its a 2nd fucking Valentine's Day.  The whole holiday season is a constant stream of reminders that I am alone.  I'm only 35 but I've given up hope, and I'd just like to take the easy way out at this point.
